item.title: Shiprocket posts maiden profit on strong core business growth
item.description: The company swung to a profit of Rs 60 lakh ($63,487) in the quarter ended September 30, from a loss of Rs 20.29 crore a year ago

item.title: India flags Chinese-linked AI tools in hacking campaign against financial firms
item.description: India's cybersecurity agency named the hacking group behind a wave of AI-driven attacks on financial firms and identified its tools, at least two of them linked to China, adding India to a growing list of countries where

item.title: Blinkit Ambulance to charge Rs 2,500 for non-emergency trips; emergency service will stay free: Deepinder Goyal
item.description: Goyal said Blinkit Ambulance has served about 42,000 cases in the last two years, of which roughly 20,000 were emergencies. None were charged but a growing share of bookings were for routine checkups, hospital visits and hospital-to-home transfers, trips that “an Uber or private transport could have handled just as easily,” he said.

item.title: China blocks SoftBank's $5.4 billion takeover of ABB's robotics division: FT
item.description: Softbank had agreed to buy ABB's robotics business in October last year, as CEO Masayoshi Son sought to establish SoftBank as a core player in the development of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Sony posts 45% Q2 profit rise on movies, games boost
item.description: Contributors to the stronger performance, which led the Japanese entertainment and technology conglomerate to hike its full-year profit outlook by 9%, included the hit movie "Spider-Man: Brand New Day".

item.title: AI to reshape India's office space demand, workforce seen at 48 million by 2030: Report
item.description: AI is expected to change the nature of India's office space demand rather than reduce it, with the country's office-using workforce projected to grow from around 38 million in 2025 to 48 million by 2030, according to a study by Cushman & Wakefield.

item.title: AI sharpens cat-and-mouse hacking battle as companies strengthen defences
item.description: From hacked supermarket fridges and a record cryptocurrency theft at Binance to an emergency over flaws in widely used web software, companies worldwide are facing a wave of cyber threats executives say AI is accelerating

item.title: Microsoft rejects multibillion-dollar AI deal with UK's Nscale
item.description: The report comes weeks after Microsoft pulled out of a deal to anchor Nscale's flagship data centre project in Loughton, Essex, after power connection delays pushed its expected supply date into the 2030s

item.title: Google unveils $15 billion data centre investment in Malaysia
item.description: Google announced plans on Wednesday to invest $15 billion in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centres and other infrastructure as demand booms for artificial intelligence services. It said the $15 billion investment will be made "over the next two years (2027 to 2028)", expanding on a $2 billion investment announced in 2024.

item.title: Google turns off AI for schoolchildren by default
item.description: Google has said it will switch off its AI tools for schoolchildren by default, after drawing criticism for pushing artificial intelligence features to students while schools are still debating how the technology should be used in classrooms. The feature was switched on by default for students at schools that had already enabled Gemini.

item.title: Figma banking on AI credits, in-house model to lift margins
item.description: Figma is leaning on cashing in on its AI features through credits and using its first-party model to power tasks on its design software platform to bolster its margins, finance chief Praveer Melwani told Reuters on Wednesday.

item.title: Australia data centre inquiry finds inadequate checks, stops short of moratorium
item.description: An inquiry into data centres by Australia's most populous state found approvals failed to consider the cumulative effect on resources and infrastructure but stopped short of calling for a moratorium, prompting a blistering rebuke from its chair.

item.title: Arm beats second-quarter revenue estimates on AI and data-center demand
item.description: Arm said its server-chip architecture accounted for more than 50% of deployments at major cloud providers in 2025 and is expected to exceed 60% by the end of 2026.

item.title: Qualcomm's smartphone chip sales miss estimates, shares fall
item.description: Demand for lucrative high-bandwidth storage for AI servers has pushed up memory chip prices, raising the cost of consumer electronics and squeezing smartphone processor designers such as Qualcomm.

item.title: OpenAI, ready to IPO in 2027, now counts majority of sales from enterprises, Greg Brockman says
item.description: OpenAI President Greg Brockman said on Wednesday the company now generates the majority of its revenue from enterprise sales and he believes it will be ready to go public in 2027.

item.title: OpenAI to acquire developer tools firm Pierre to expand Codex capabilities
item.description: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company, the developer of open-source coding tools, to expand its Codex platform's capabilities in building, understanding and reviewing software, as it looks to strengthen the role of AI agents across the software development process.

item.title: Apple cuts employee AI budgets in cost-control push
item.description: Apple has reduced employee budgets for AI usage as part of a broader effort to rein in costs, even as it seeks to expand the use of AI across its operations, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Goldman, Apollo seek buyers for $40 billion SpaceX AI chip deal
item.description: Goldman Sachs and Apollo Global Management are in talks with investors to sell portions of a roughly $40 billion financing deal for SpaceX's AI chips, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday.

item.title: Lenskart, Nykaa, PhysicsWallah see Q2 profits surge
item.description: New-age companies Nykaa, Lenskart, and PhysicsWallah reported strong numbers for the September quarter. This and more in today’s ETtech Top 5.

item.title: Uber's profit forecast disappoints as driver shortages, Middle East conflict hurt
item.description: The company is responding by spending more to recruit and retain drivers, a cost that will be watched closely because it comes as the company also funds a major push into autonomous vehicles and a string of acquisitions.

item.title: Tech funding hits 12-month low of $592 million in October; late-stage funding plunges 72%
item.description: Early-stage funding, by contrast, rose 114% sequentially to $361.6 million from $168.6 million and was up 10.8% from $326.4 million in October 2025. Early-stage rounds accounted for 61% of the month's funding.

item.title: AMD shares jump as AI-driven data-center strength fuels growth outlook
item.description: AMD, which recently joined the ranks of trillion-dollar companies, has gained about 126% this year and is poised to add about $58 billion in market value if premarket gains hold. The company's strong outlook highlighted growing momentum in its server processor business, signaling that spending on AI computing was extending beyond Nvidia's accelerators, which dominate the market.

item.title: 70% of global business leaders report rising risk exposure amid AI, geopolitical disruptions: KPMG
item.description: According to the report, 56% of respondents said external disruptions involving geopolitical, energy, cyber, trade or climate-related factors would cause severe operational disruptions or significantly affect their organisations' costs and performance over the next three to five years.

item.title: Singapore Airlines says 46,000 booking records affected by Amadeus breach
item.description: Singapore Airlines said on Tuesday that about 46,000 booking records may have been ​affected by a cybersecurity incident involving Amadeus, its reservation technology

item.title: Oracle abandons $7 billion Tencent AI deal under Trump pressure: FT
item.description: US officials approached Oracle to raise concerns about the Tencent deal, the newspaper said, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Google extends voluntary buyout offers to employees in several countries
item.description: The move comes amid mounting AI spending that has unnerved Wall Street and dented Alphabet's stock price. Microsoft last week offered voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees in an effort to contain costs. Alphabet's workforce has grown steadily in recent quarters, but it has sought to shift resources toward priority areas.

item.title: SK Hynix's New York chip plans hit snag over US restrictions on China, sources say
item.description: SK Hynix is seeking US export licenses to equip its Dalian plant, arguing that increased production there would help fund its planned US expansion. But the Commerce Department has yet to approve the new licenses, the people said. Its Solidigm unit plans to invest about $45 billion and build two NAND plants in Marcy, New York, two people said, with investment potentially reaching about $100 billion over time. NAND is memory that retains data even when power is turned off and is used for storage in data centers.

item.title: AMD forecasts quarterly revenue above estimates as data-center growth accelerates
item.description: The company, which nearly doubled its data-center revenue in the third quarter, is benefiting as a shift in AI workloads toward running models in real-world applications drives demand for its graphics processing units and central processors. This has enabled AMD to capture market share from rival Intel, which last week forecast quarterly revenue well below estimates and triggered a global selloff in chip stocks.

item.title: AMD's OpenAI, Meta chip deals trigger $1 billion quarterly charge
item.description: AMD in February agreed to sell up to $60 billion worth of AI chips to Meta over five years, giving the Facebook owner warrants that could let it buy as much as 10% of the chip firm if it meets certain milestones. The deal followed a similar agreement with OpenAI last year, giving the startup the option to buy up to roughly 10% of the chipmaker.

item.title: IndiaAI Mission's three indigenous AI models target offline mobile access, secure use in critical sectors
item.description: Three indigenous artificial intelligence (AI) models launched under the Centre's IndiaAI Mission are being developed for applications ranging from offline access on mobile phones to secure use in critical sectors such as defence, cybersecurity and banking.

item.title: Gig workers may get social security benefits through 2% transaction levy on businesses
item.description: The government is considering implementing a 2% transaction-based levy on aggregators to support social security for gig workers. This levy will fund benefits such as insurance, health, and maternity support for over 12 million workers. There is a consensus that this approach ensures fairness among different types of aggregators. The new scheme is expected to be launched in 2027, requiring gig workers to meet specific work criteria.

item.title: Meta raises $15 billion in five-part US bond sale
item.description: The tech giant's offering adds to a wave of fundraising as companies raise fresh capital to finance AI data centers, computing capacity and cloud expansion, despite traditionally relying on cash-rich balance sheets to fund growth.

item.title: Human control must set limits on superintelligence, says OpenAI's Sam Altman
item.description: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman has said that human control over the future must remain a fundamental condition for artificial intelligence (AI) development, arguing that people should not surrender decision-making power to increasingly advanced AI systems.

item.title: Google will cut off search access for students at schools that reject AI
item.description: The Mountain View, California, company has been facing pushback from educators, child development experts and parents over the use of its technology in schools, with the backlash heating up since it announced in August that it had turned on its Gemini chatbot for many K-12 students who use Google Classroom.

item.title: Tesla misled South Korean customers about automated-driving tech, consumer group alleges
item.description: Tesla has marketed Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software to prospective buyers in South Korea for years, often collecting lump-sum payments of 9.043 million won ($6,726).

item.title: AMD's OpenAI, Meta chip deals trigger $1 billion quarterly charge
item.description: AMD in February agreed to sell up to $60 billion worth of AI chips to Meta over five years, giving the Facebook owner warrants that could let it buy as much as 10% of the chip firm if it meets certain milestones. The deal followed a similar agreement with OpenAI last year, giving the startup the option to buy up to roughly 10% of the chipmaker.

item.title: Canva to cut about 22% of staff as growth slowdown triggers restructuring
item.description: Australian graphic design platform Canva Group said on Wednesday it would cut 1,271 jobs, or about 22% of its workforce, as part of a restructuring after growth slowed for the first time in a decade.

item.title: Premji's deeptech bets; Razorpay gets IPO nod
item.description: Happy Thursday! Premji Invest is stepping up its bets on defence and aerospace manufacturing.This and more in today’s ETtech Morning Dispatch.

item.title: Apple’s robust India quarter; Giva’s $100 million funding
item.description: Apple posted record sales in India in the September quarter. This and more in today’s ETtech Top 5.

item.title: Samsung to make AMD, Nvidia chip parts at second Texas plant: Report
item.description: Construction is due to start formally this month, with the plant having secured orders for its entire output, and most of the secured volume is for AMD, according to Maeil.

item.title: China's 'Lipstick King' touts AI tokens in first for Singles' Day festival
item.description: The launch is the first time AI token packages have been offered as a significant consumer product category during Singles' Day, the world's largest shopping festival originally held on November 11 each year.

item.title: Oracle plans to raise $20 billion through bonds and stock sales
item.description: The company said last week that it expects capital spending to peak this fiscal year and the next as it builds more cloud-computing capacity, but pledged to raise no more than $20 billion in additional financing for AI through fiscal 2030.

item.title: Binance co-CEO says company is in very strong financial health after $6.3 billion heist
item.description: Teng told a Hong Kong Fintech Week event Binance's hourly inflows and outflows had "pretty much normalised" and 95% of the affected tokens had been replenished.

item.title: Global markets were already fragile. Big AI bets could break them
item.description: Investors flocked to bonds. Yields, which move inversely to price, fell from multidecade highs, with the benchmark 10-year Treasury, which guides borrowing costs globally, falling almost 20 basis points on October 22, its biggest daily fall since early 2023.

item.title: Reddit blasts Australia's 'inept' social media ban as court challenge begins
item.description: Australia's world-first teen social media ban was "ill thought out" and amounted to a "profound restriction on political debate", a lawyer for messaging platform Reddit told the country's top court in the first legal challenge to the law.

item.title: From SBI to Binance, how financial institutions are becoming cyberattack targets
item.description: Recent incidents involving cryptocurrency exchange Binance and Indian public sector lender State Bank of India (SBI) have once again put the spotlight on the issue. While Binance reported a security breach involving unauthorised cryptocurrency withdrawals estimated at around $6.3 billion, SBI is investigating a suspected data leak involving nearly 3,900 customer records.

item.title: Singapore's Grab lifts 2026 forecasts on strong ride-hailing, delivery demand
item.description: Singapore's Grab lifted its annual forecasts on Tuesday, helped by steady growth in its ride-hailing unit, while demand for its delivery services benefited from promotional offers and expansion into categories beyond groceries.

item.title: Blackstone president says more tech sector fundraising ahead to keep up with AI industry growth
item.description: Blackstone President Jon Gray said on Tuesday there would be more global equity fundraising needed to keep up with the enormous likely demand from the AI industry's growth.

item.title: Anthropic says revenue surged 1,100% ahead of IPO
item.description: Anthropic, one of the world's leading artificial intelligence companies, on Monday reported a more than 1,100 percent surge in quarterly revenue and nearly $900 billion in spending commitments as it counts down to its Wall Street listing later this month. The filing said the company has committed to spend about $895 billion, mostly on computing power, with $70 billion of that due before September 2027.

item.title: Binance to reopen withdrawals for more assets on several networks
item.description: Binance said on Monday it will reopen withdrawals for more assets on networks, including BSC, ETH, SOL, XRP and SUI. The reopenings will begin at 04:00 GMT on Tuesday, the company added.
